Lesson information

Level: A0, children
Time: 60 minutes
Dialect: British

Phonics: S /s/, A /æ/, T /t/

Goal: can recognise the sounds /s/, /æ/ and /t/, connect each sound to its letter, and identify familiar words beginning with these sounds

Speaking: can hear, identify and produce the target sounds and match them to the letters S, A and T

Writing: can recognise, trace and write uppercase and lowercase letters S, s, A, a, T, t

Blending: can blend individual sounds to read simple CVC words

Lead-in

Show the closed curtain.

Say, “Look! What’s behind the curtain? Let’s see!”

Do not ask the child to name the letters yet.

Point to each pair, model only the sound and invite the child to repeat: “/s/”, “/æ/”, “/t/”.

Support for less confident students:

Use a clear mouth position and a hand cue for each sound.

Let the child repeat together with you before saying the sound alone.

Fast finishers extension:

Point to the three letter pairs in a random order and let the child produce the sound without a model.

Ученику скрыта

Letters

Show one letter pair at a time with numbered strokes and arrows.

Say, “Big S, little s”, then “Big A, little a”, then “Big T, little t”.

The child repeats the letter names.

Trace each model with your finger first.

Then complete the first trace together with the pen tool.

Support for less confident students:

Keep the stroke model visible. Let the child trace over a dotted letter before copying it into an empty space. Guide the first stroke verbally: “Start here. Down / round / across.”

Fast finishers extension:

After tracing, hide the stroke arrows and ask the child to write one uppercase and one lowercase letter from memory.
